about.size: Common at about 5-15 lb; can reach about 37 in and 30 lb
about.depth: 25-95 m, usually 40-70 m (FishBase); adults deeper than juveniles
about.behavior: Adults live on reefs, ledges and around wrecks and artificial reefs, often patrolling the edge between reef and sand. Juveniles use seagrass and mangroves.
about.spawning: Forms large spawning aggregations on reef promontories along the shelf edge, building the week before the full moon, with spawning 2-5 days after it in the late afternoon. Season is roughly May to August in Florida.
about.regulations_note: Mutton snapper have size limits, and some areas protect spawning aggregations. Check FWC rules.
about.timing_note: Angler lore: patterns reported by local captains and fishing writers, not tested by studies. Numbers are judgment calls to be calibrated against trip logs. Reports disagree on mutton snapper: some captains say day trips, others night.
